newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct hog prices early Thursday were steady to mostly $0.50-$1.00 per cwt higher as packers competed for tight hog supplies, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Demand for hogs was intense, even with slaughter cutbacks at many plants, as hog marketings receded, they said.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs sold steady to $1.00 higher at $55.00 to $56.00 in the country and $56.00 to $57.50 at plants. Illinois hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 higher at $55.00 to $56.00 in the country and $57.00 to $57.50 at plants. Some sources there said prices could be even higher.
Indiana hogs sold up $0.50, but could go higher as the day progressed, with $55.00 paid in the country and $56.50 at plants.
At least one major packer buyer in Indiana said weights were running current at 240 to 250 lbs, suggesting that farmers were not holding hogs back.
Ohio hogs sold $1.00 higher at $53.00 to $54.00 in the country and $55.00 at plants, with many farmers contracting the "corn planting disease," one dealer said.
"They'll be out there farming as long as the weather allows," the dealer said.
